diff --git a/powershell/internal/services/azure/Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath.ps1 b/powershell/internal/services/azure/Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath.ps1
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..f68017821
--- /dev/null
+++ b/powershell/internal/services/azure/Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath.ps1
@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+﻿function Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns the Microsoft Defender for Cloud attack paths grouped by path, together with whether
+    Defender CSPM is enabled on any readable subscription.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Attack paths are computed by Defender CSPM, so an empty result has two very different meanings:
+    the plan is off and nothing was ever computed, or the plan is on and the estate genuinely has no
+    path. The returned object separates them. CspmEnabled comes from the Defender for Cloud pricing of
+    CloudPosture, which Azure Resource Graph exposes as microsoft.security/pricings, so the caller can
+    report "not licensed" instead of a pass.
+
+    On the fields, measured against a live Defender CSPM subscription rather than assumed:
+
+    - properties.attackPathType is a GUID and properties.displayName is a sentence. The engine
+      requires an instance ID matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$, so the GUID is the ID of
+      the path type and the sentence is the title. Grouping by the GUID is also what "one result per
+      attack path type" means: the sentence can repeat across occurrences of the same type.
+    - properties.entryPoint carries entityInternalId, entityType and dataSource, and no entity name,
+      so the entry point is reported by its resource type.
+    - properties.target does carry entityName as well as entityType, so the target is named.
+    - properties.riskFactors and properties.mITRETacticsAndTechniques.tactics are arrays. Azure
+      Resource Graph does not support mv-apply, so they are carried as their JSON text and parsed
+      here.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath
+
+    Returns whether Defender CSPM is on and the attack paths grouped by path.
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
+    param()
+
+    $pricingQuery = @'
+securityresources
+| where type == "microsoft.security/pricings"
+| where name == "CloudPosture"
+| summarize StandardCount = countif(tostring(properties.pricingTier) == "Standard")
+'@
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Checking whether Defender CSPM is enabled...'
+    $pricing = @(Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest -Query $pricingQuery) | Select-Object -First 1
+    $cspmEnabled = $null -ne $pricing -and [int]($pricing.StandardCount) -gt 0
+
+    $pathQuery = @'
+securityresources
+| where type == "microsoft.security/attackpaths"
+| extend nombre = tostring(properties.displayName),
+         riesgo = tostring(properties.riskLevel),
+         parcial = tostring(properties.isPartialAttackPath),
+         factores = tostring(properties.riskFactors),
+         tacticas = tostring(properties.mITRETacticsAndTechniques.tactics),
+         tipoEntrada = tostring(properties.entryPoint.entityType),
+         nombreDestino = tostring(properties.target.entityName),
+         tipoDestino = tostring(properties.target.entityType)
+// A risk level is per occurrence, so a group holds several. any() picked one at random, and it
+// picked independently for the risk factors and the tactics, so the three could describe different
+// occurrences of the same attack path type. arg_max takes all three from the one that ranks worst.
+| extend rangoRiesgo = case(riesgo =~ "Critical", 4, riesgo =~ "High", 3, riesgo =~ "Medium", 2, riesgo =~ "Low", 1, 0)
+| summarize PathCount = count(),
+            DisplayName = any(nombre),
+            Partial = any(parcial),
+            EntryPointTypeList = make_set(tipoEntrada, 10),
+            TargetList = make_set(nombreDestino, 10),
+            // make_set is capped, so the consumer needs to know when it is showing a subset.
+            TargetTotal = dcount(nombreDestino),
+            TargetTypeList = make_set(tipoDestino, 10),
+            (RiskRank, RiskLevel, RiskFactorsJson, TacticsJson) = arg_max(rangoRiesgo, riesgo, factores, tacticas)
+    by AttackPathType = tostring(properties.attackPathType)
+| project-away RiskRank
+| sort by PathCount desc, AttackPathType asc
+'@
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Querying Defender for Cloud attack paths...'
+    $rows = @(Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest -Query $pathQuery)
+
+    function ConvertFrom-MtJsonArray {
+        param([string] $Text)
+        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Text)) { return @() }
+        try { return @($Text | ConvertFrom-Json) } catch { return @() }
+    }
+
+    $paths = [System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]]::new()
+    foreach ($row in $rows) {
+        if (-not $row -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$row.AttackPathType)) { continue }
+        $paths.Add([pscustomobject]@{
+                AttackPathType     = [string]$row.AttackPathType
+                DisplayName        = [string]$row.DisplayName
+                RiskLevel          = [string]$row.RiskLevel
+                PathCount          = [int]($row.PathCount)
+                RiskFactorList     = ConvertFrom-MtJsonArray -Text ([string]$row.RiskFactorsJson)
+                TacticList         = ConvertFrom-MtJsonArray -Text ([string]$row.TacticsJson)
+                EntryPointTypeList = @($row.EntryPointTypeList | Where-Object { $_ })
+                TargetList         = @($row.TargetList | Where-Object { $_ })
+                TargetTotal        = [int]($row.TargetTotal)
+                TargetTypeList     = @($row.TargetTypeList | Where-Object { $_ })
+            })
+    }
+
+    [pscustomobject]@{
+        CspmEnabled = $cspmEnabled
+        PathList    = $paths
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+﻿function Get-MtDefenderForCloudRecommendation {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns one row per Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendation across the subscriptions the
+    signed-in account can read, with how many resources are healthy, unhealthy, not applicable and
+    exempt.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Runs a single Azure Resource Graph query over securityresources, aggregated server side so the
+    result is one row per recommendation rather than one row per resource and recommendation. A large
+    estate produces thousands of assessment rows and only hundreds of recommendations, which is the
+    difference the caller needs to stay readable.
+
+    Each row carries the recommendation's assessment key, display name, severity from its metadata, the
+    risk level Defender CSPM adds when it is enabled, the portal link, the resource counts, a capped
+    sample of the unhealthy resource names, and the exemption cause when every resource is exempt.
+
+    An empty result means Defender for Cloud produced no assessment for these subscriptions. The caller
+    must skip in that case: no unhealthy resource over no assessment is not a pass.
+
+    Errors are deliberately not caught here, so a failed query surfaces instead of being read as a
+    clean estate.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtDefenderForCloudRecommendation
+
+    Returns the Defender for Cloud recommendations with their resource counts.
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]])]
+    param()
+
+    $query = @'
+securityresources
+| where type == "microsoft.security/assessments"
+// Multicloud connectors surface AWS and GCP assessments in the same table, and their counts
+// would flow into an Azure test. Native Azure resources have no Source, so the empty string is
+// kept deliberately: filtering on Source == "Azure" alone would return nothing.
+| extend origen = tostring(properties.resourceDetails.Source)

+﻿function Get-MtAzureDefenderForCloudRecommendationInstance {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns one MT.1257 instance per Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendation.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Instance source of the MT.1257 family. The suffix is the recommendation's assessment key
+    (MT.1257.<assessmentKey>) and the title names the recommendation, the way MT.1024 does for Entra
+    recommendations. One instance per recommendation, never one per resource: a large estate produces
+    thousands of assessment rows and only hundreds of recommendations.
+
+    When Defender for Cloud returns no assessment at all the source emits nothing and the engine skips
+    the family with NoInstances. A subscription with no assessment has no recommendation to comply
+    with, and must never be reported as having none unhealthy.
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
+    param()
+
+    $recommendations = Get-MtDefenderForCloudRecommendation
+
+    foreach ($recommendation in $recommendations) {
+        if ($recommendation.TotalCount -le 0) { continue }
+
+        $name = if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($recommendation.DisplayName)) {
+            $recommendation.AssessmentKey
+        } else {
+            $recommendation.DisplayName
+        }
+
+        $source = if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($recommendation.RiskLevel)) { $recommendation.RiskLevel } else { $recommendation.Severity }
+        $severity = switch -Regex ($source) {
+            '^(Critical|High)$' { 'High'; break }
+            '^Medium$'          { 'Medium'; break }
+            '^Low$'             { 'Low'; break }
+            default             { 'Medium' }
+        }
+
+        [pscustomobject]@{
+            Id       = $recommendation.AssessmentKey
+            Title    = "No resource should be left unhealthy for the Defender for Cloud recommendation '$name'."
+            Severity = $severity
+            Data     = $recommendation
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+function Test-MtAzureDefenderForCloudRecommendation {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Ensure no resource is left unhealthy for a Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendation.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Defender for Cloud assesses the resources of every subscription it covers against a catalogue of
+    recommendations and reports, per recommendation, which resources are healthy. An assessor normally
+    reads that one recommendation at a time in the Azure portal. This check brings it into a Maester
+    run.
+
+    It runs once per recommendation, following the InstanceSource pattern MT.1024 introduced. A
+    recommendation passes when no resource is unhealthy and fails when any is, with the resource
+    counts, a sample of the unhealthy resource names and the portal link to the full list.
+
+    Severity follows the source, as #2510 asks. Defender CSPM adds a risk level per recommendation,
+    and that is preferred when present; otherwise the recommendation's own metadata severity is used.
+
+    A recommendation whose resources are all exempt is skipped with the exemption cause, so a decision
+    already recorded in the Azure portal is respected rather than reported again. A recommendation that
+    applies to nothing is skipped as not applicable. Neither is reported as a pass.
+
+    .OUTPUTS
+    [bool] - True when no resource is unhealthy, false when any is, null when skipped.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Test-MtAzureDefenderForCloudRecommendation
+
+    Returns one result per Defender for Cloud recommendation.
+
+    .LINK
+    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtAzureDefenderForCloudRecommendation
+    [MaesterTest(
+        Id = 'MT.1257',
+        Title = 'Resources should be healthy for the Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendations.',
+        Product = 'azure',
+        Feature = 'subscriptions',
+        Area = 'infrastructure',
+        ResourceType = 'AzureResource',
+        Severity = 'Medium',
+        UserImpact = 'Low',
+        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',

merill
### Goal

Microsoft already scores and ranks many risks in its own portals: Secure Score, Defender for Cloud, Defender Vulnerability Management, Entra ID Protection, Exposure Management. An assessor today has to visit each portal. Maester should be able to pull these signals in, based on what the tenant is licensed for, so one Maester run can be the single place to review a tenant's security posture.

### Decided

- **Opt-in, not on by default.** These sources do not run in a default `Invoke-Maester`. Users turn them on explicitly (for example as built-in opt-in packs or a config/parameter switch; the exact mechanism is decided during implementation).
- **New permissions are opt-in too.** The default scopes in `Get-MtGraphScope` / `Connect-Maester` do not change. The extra permissions (`SecurityEvents.Read.All` for Secure Score; `IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All` and `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All` for ID Protection; any Defender for Endpoint API scope) are only requested when the user opts in to the sources that need them.

### Principles

- **License-aware.** Each source declares the `License` and `Service` it needs. A tenant without the licence gets a Skipped result with the reason "not licensed", never a failure.
- **One result per recommendation**, using the `InstanceSource` pattern MT.1024 introduced, so each Microsoft recommendation shows up as its own row with its own severity and remediation link.
- **Status mapping is consistent across sources:**
  - Completed / Healthy / score at max → Passed
  - Active / Unhealthy / below max → Failed
  - Not applicable → Skipped (not applicable)
  - Dismissed, risk accepted, resolved by third party or alternate mitigation in the Microsoft portal → Skipped, with the portal's reason, so Maester respects decisions already made there
  - Product not licensed → Skipped (not licensed)
- **Severity comes from the source** (Secure Score rank and max score, Defender for Cloud severity or risk level), mapped to Maester's Severity scale.
- **No double counting.** Where a Maester check already covers the same control, the report shows one finding and links the two (#2512).
- **Read-only.** Only reader permissions, no changes in the tenant or subscription.

### Open questions (decide during implementation)

- **Opt-in mechanism.** Built-in opt-in packs (one per source, selected with `-Pack`), a config setting, or a parameter on `Invoke-Maester` / `Connect-Maester`?
- **Volume.** Large Azure estates can return thousands

+let assessed = toscalar(DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | summarize dcount(DeviceId));

+| where VulnerabilitySeverityLevel in ('High', 'Critical')

+    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB

+﻿function Get-MtDefenderSecureConfigurationAssessment {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns one row per Defender Vulnerability Management security configuration, with how many devices
+    it applies to and how many of those are not compliant with it.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Runs a single advanced hunting query over DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessment, joined to
+    DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessmentKB for the configuration's name, description, risk and impact.
+    The aggregation happens server side, so the result is one row per configuration rather than one row
+    per device and configuration.
+
+    Only configurations Defender reports as applicable to at least one device are returned. A
+    configuration that applies to nothing cannot be complied with or breached, so it has no outcome to
+    judge.
+
+    An empty result means Defender Vulnerability Management has no assessment data for this tenant,
+    typically because no device is onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. The caller must skip in that case:
+    "no configuration is non-compliant" over zero assessed configurations is not a pass.
+
+    Errors are deliberately not caught here. Invoke-MtGraphSecurityQuery throws on a query execution
+    error, and letting that surface keeps a broken query from being reported as a clean tenant.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtDefenderSecureConfigurationAssessment
+
+    Returns the security configurations assessed in the tenant with their non-compliant device counts.
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]])]
+    param()
+
+    $query = @'
+DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessment
+| where IsApplicable == true
+| summarize ApplicableDeviceCount = dcount(DeviceId),
+            NonCompliantDeviceCount = dcountif(DeviceId, IsCompliant == false),
+            NonCompliantDeviceList = make_set_if(DeviceName, IsCompliant == false, 10),
+            ConfigurationCategory = any(ConfigurationCategory),
+            ConfigurationSubcategory = any(ConfigurationSubcategory)
+    by ConfigurationId
+| join kind=leftouter (
+    DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessmentKB
+    | project ConfigurationId, ConfigurationName, ConfigurationDescription, RiskDescription, ConfigurationImpact
+  ) on ConfigurationId
+| project-away ConfigurationId1
+| sort by NonCompliantDeviceCount desc, ConfigurationImpact desc

+
+    Errors are deliberately not caught here, so a failed query surfaces instead of being read as an
+    estate with no score.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtAzureSecureScore
+
+    Returns the secure score and compliance standards of each readable subscription.
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]])]
+    param()
+
+    $scoreQuery = @'
+securityresources
+| where type == "microsoft.security/securescores"
+| where name == "ascScore"
+| extend currentScore = todouble(properties.score.current),
+         maxScore = todouble(properties.score.max),
+         initiative = tostring(properties.displayName)
+| project subscriptionId, currentScore, maxScore, initiative
+| sort by subscriptionId asc
+'@
+
+    $standardQuery = @'
+securityresources
+| where type == "microsoft.security/regulatorycompliancestandards"
+| extend standard = name,
+         state = tostring(properties.state),
+         passedControls = toint(properties.passedControls),
+         failedControls = toint(properties.failedControls),
+         skippedControls = toint(properties.skippedControls),
+         unsupportedControls = toint(properties.unsupportedControls)
+| project subscriptionId, standard, state, passedControls, failedControls, skippedControls, unsupportedControls
+| sort by subscriptionId asc, standard asc
+'@
+
+    $nameQuery = @'
+resourcecontainers
+| where type == "microsoft.resources/subscriptions"
+| project subscriptionId, subscriptionName = name
+'@
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Querying the Defender for Cloud secure score through Azure Resource Graph...'
+    $scoreRows = @(Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest -Query $scoreQuery)
+
+    $result = [System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]]::new()
+    if ($scoreRows.Count -eq 0) {
+        Write-Output $result -NoEnumerate
+        return
+    }
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Querying the regulatory compliance standards...'
+    $standardRows = @(Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest -Query $standardQuery)
+    Write-Verbose 'Querying the subscription names...'
+    $nameRows = @(Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest -Query $nameQuery)
+
+    $nameLookup = @{}
+    foreach ($row in $nameRows) {
+        if (-not $row -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$row.subscriptionId)) { continue }
+        $nameLookup[[string]$row.subscriptionId] = [string]$row.subscriptionName
+    }
+
+    $standardLookup = @{}
+    foreach ($row in $standardRows) {
+        if (-not $row -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$row.subscriptionId)) { continue }
+        $id = [string]$row.subscriptionId
+        if (-not $standardLookup.ContainsKey($id)) {
+            $standardLookup[$id] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[pscustomobject]]::new()
+        }
+        $standardLookup[$id].Add([pscustomobject]@{
+                Standard            = [string]$row.standard
+                State               = [string]$row.state
+                PassedControls      = [int]($row.passedControls)
+                FailedControls      = [int]($row.failedControls)
+                SkippedControls     = [int]($row.skippedControls)
+                UnsupportedControls = [int]($row.unsupportedControls)
+            })
+    }
+
+    foreach ($row in $scoreRows) {
+        if (-not $row -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$row.subscriptionId)) { continue }
+        $id = [string]$row.subscriptionId
+        $current = [double]($row.currentScore)
+        $max = [double]($row.maxScore)
+        $percentage = if ($max -gt 0) { [math]::Round(($current / $max) * 100, 1) } else { $null }
+
+        $result.Add([pscustomobject]@{
+                SubscriptionId   = $id
+                SubscriptionName = if ($nameLookup.ContainsKey($id)) { $nameLookup[$id] } else { $id }
+                Initiative       = [string]$row.initiative
+                CurrentScore     = $current
+                MaxScore         = $max
+                ScorePercentage  = $percentage
+                StandardList     = if ($standardLookup.ContainsKey($id)) { @($standardLookup[$id]) } else { @() }
+            })
+    }
+
+    Write-Output $result -NoEnumerate
+}

content.content:
Rate every value for a typical organization that fails the test, using the fix the test's own Markdown file
recommends. Do not rate for the best case, the worst case or one tenant you know. When two values fit, choose the
lower one for `Severity`, `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost`. A reader should be able to see the reason for
each value in the test's description and remediation text.

## Product

The product where the fix is made. One value.

- Use the product whose admin surface holds the setting, not every product the test reads from.
- Tests in a product folder (`tests/maester/entra`, `tests/cisa/exchange`) use that folder's product.
- A product the test only reads from, or a licence it needs, is not a second product. `Service` and `License`
  already say that.

## RelatedProduct

Other products the test also checks or depends on. Optional list, never the same key as `Product`.

- Add one when an admin of that product would expect to find the test under it. An Exchange Online test about an
  anti-phishing policy that is managed in the Defender portal has `RelatedProduct = 'defender'`.
- Add one when the fix is made in that product's portal although the test lives in another product's folder.
- Do not add a product only because its API is called.

## Feature

The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

None of the four PRs is ready to merge. Three of them use MT IDs that someone else reserved first, and MT.1253 conflicts with a design ruling in #2683.

**What applies to all four**
- **ID clash.** Cloud-Architekt reserved MT.1253–1258 on #697 on 2026-10-28. His open draft PR #2705 uses those same files under `tests/maester/entra/`. PRs 2694 (1253/1254), 2695 (1255/1256) and 2703 (1257/1258) have to renumber from MT.1267 up and reserve the new IDs on #697. MT.1266 (2712) was reserved properly.
- **These are sanctioned as tests.** They implement children of merill's epic #2510: #2519, #2517, #2514/#2516 and #2515. The epic decided "one result per recommendation" with InstanceSource and severity taken from the source, so building them as test families is right. The epic also says opt-in. All of them set `Lifecycle='Preview'`, so they don't run by default today, which covers it for now.
- **No comments from merill** on any of the four. The CodeRabbit check reports neutral on 2712, 2703 and 2695 and reports nothing on 2694; on all four, every review thread is resolved. The attribute-review workflow passed on all four. No other CI ran on 2694's latest head (e9f128b).
- **Merge order.** All four edit `powershell/tests/fixtures/golden/selection.json`, so each will need a rebase after the one before it lands. All four are BEHIND main.

**2694: Intune compliance and baselines (MT.1253/1254). Verdict: HOLD-FOR-DESIGN**
- **Design clash.** MT.1253 ("non-compliant share ≤ 5%") is the `devices-compliant` measure in #2683. Section 11 of the design doc records merill's ruling of 5 Nov: "A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration… must not change pass rates." #2519, written earlier, asked for it as a test, so merill has to say which one stands.
- **Defect.** In `Get-MtSecurityBaseline.ps1:39`, MT.1254 reads only the legacy `deviceManagement/templates` baselines. New baselines are settings-catalog `configurationPolicies` with a baseline `templateReference`, which #2519 itself names. A tenant on current baselines gets NoInstances and is skipped silently.
- **Nit.** There is no `Permission` attribute.

> Thanks @earbona23, the evidence runs are really useful. Two blockers: MT.1253–1258 are reserved by Cloud-Architekt on #697 (and used in #2705), so please renumber from MT.1267. And MT.1254 only reads the legacy `deviceManagement/templates` baselines; please add the settings-catalog baselines (`configurationPolicies` with a baseline templateReference, as #2519 notes). MT.1253 overlaps the `devices-compliant` measure in #2683; holding it until merill says whether it stays a test.

**2695: Defender vulnerability management (MT.1255/1256). Verdict: CHANGES**
The KQL is aggregated on the server, and it goes through the cached `Invoke-MtGraphSecurityQuery` helper, which uses the `ThreatHunting.Read.All` scope we already request. The fix for the severity going on the instance object is correct.
- **Defect.** Device names and the knowledge-base description text are written without `Get-MtSafeMarkdown`: `Test.MT.1255.ps1:131,136,140` and `Test.MT.1256.ps1:95`. That is the #2711 class.
- **Overlap.** MT.1256 is a superset of MT.1087 (xspm). It is distinct enough to keep, because it has no internet-exposure condition, but the guide should link to MT.1087.
- **Nit.** "up to ten shown" gives no total.

Draft comment:
> Nice work. Please renumber (1255/1256 are reserved on #697), run device names and the KB description/risk text through `Get-MtSafeMarkdown`, and mention MT.1087 in the 1256 guide so readers see how the two differ.

**2703: Defender for Cloud recommendations and attack paths (MT.1257/1258). Verdict: CHANGES**
Uses ARG through `Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest`, which pages, and the worst-risk ranking is a good fix.
- **ID clash** (above).
- **Defect.** Unhealthy resource names and attack-path target names are written raw: `Test.MT.1257.ps1:155` and `Test.MT.1258.ps1:119`.
- **Defect.** A nested `function ConvertFrom-MtJsonArray` is defined inside the helper (`Get-MtDefenderForCloudAttackPath.ps1:82`), which breaks the one-function-per-file rule.
- **Nit.** Spanish identifiers in the KQL and PowerShell (`nombre`, `severidad`, `etiquetaRecursos`). English, please.
- **Nit.** `split(id,"/")[8]` (`Get-MtDefenderForCloudRecommendation.ps1:57`) comes back empty for subscription-scope assessments.
- **Nit.** `RelatedProduct='defender'` is missing. MT.1266 has it, and the rubric says to add it when a Defender admin would look there.

Draft comment:
> Thanks! Please renumber (1257/1258 are reserved on #697), escape resource and target names with `Get-MtSafeMarkdown`, move `ConvertFrom-MtJsonArray` into its own file or inline it, switch the identifiers to English, and add `RelatedProduct = 'defender'` to match MT.1266.

**2712: Azure secure score per subscription (MT.1266). Verdict: MERGE-WITH-NIT**
The ID is reserved, the `ascScore` name filter is in place, subscription names are escaped, `Permission` is declared, attributes pass, and it is exactly what #2515 asks for.
- **Nit.** CodeRabbit's note sitting outside the diff is still unfixed. `Get-MtAzureSecureScore.ps1:120` rounds to one decimal before the `-ge` check at `Test.MT.1266.ps1:111`, so 79.96% passes an 80% target. Compare the unrounded value and round only for display.
- **Design note, not a blocker.** A score against a target sits close to #2683's "measure" idea and double-counts MT.1257 (#2512). merill should decide whether it stays a test or becomes the #2513 scores panel.

Draft comment:
> Looks good. One fix: compare the unrounded percentage against the target and round only in the output, otherwise 79.96% passes an 80% target.
